_comment: Triage fixtures for maximum-effort, from real work with the details filed off. `size` lists every acceptable size; `floor` is the worker floor the rule must produce. `tag` drives the hard constraints in run.mjs: a `routine` case must never floor at opus, a `hard` case always must, a `design` case always must floor at fable. `design` cases are steps that decide how something looks or feels (layout, colour, typography, spacing, motion, the shape of a UI surface) — they run on the Fable worker whatever the size, and fable wins even when the step is also risky (design+risky still floors fable, not opus). Wiring an existing, already-designed component to real data is NOT design — that near-miss is tagged `standard`/`sonnet` to prove the rule doesn't over-trigger. `tag: "forge"` cases exercise the '## When not to run' stand-down rule instead of size/floor: `expectForge: true` means forge state exists (wiki/plan.md or wiki/.forge/) and no by-name maximum-effort ask, so the model must answer the single word `forge`; `expectForge: false` is the escape hatch inverted — forge state exists but the user asked for maximum effort by name, so the rule must NOT stand down and a normal `size`/`floor` answer is still graded. Add a case whenever a real task was mis-sized, mis-floored, or mis-routed on the stand-down rule — the miss becomes the regression test.
